newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Bullish Estonian shares surge higher.
newsitem.headline: Bullish Estonian shares surge higher.

text.p: Shares on the Estonian stock market surged on Friday, showing no worries over a government crisis in the Baltic state.
The Tallinn stock exchange index climbed 1.57 percent to 112.67 and the official list turned over 15.3 million kroons.
The market was unruffled by news the government coalition collapsed, saying politics were having no effect on the market.
Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi is currently holding talks on forming a new government.
Market leader Hansapank was most active on trade of 7.9 million kroons.
Hansapank closed almost one kroon higher at 109.25 kroons versus 108.30 kroons.
"Hansapank shares are attractive for investors who have a long-term interest," Forekspank dealer Tonu Vanajuur said.
Second largest bank Savings Bank maintained its recent rise.
It climbed to 57.50 kroons from 54.30 kroons and traded 2.8 million kroons of stock.
"This rise is still a reflection of the last share issue which was well over-subscribed," Vanajuur added.
The market was also encouraged by news that Savings Bank subsidiary Estonian Insurance collected a healthy 17.9 million kroons in premiums in October.
The free market was dominated by the Kalev confectionary company which turned over 2.5 million kroons and ended slightly higher at 596 kroons.
Total over-the-counter trade was 6.2 million kroons.
